title: Line index
description: index.json. One entry per line with headline numbers, so the homepage and line search need no other file. Lines with no measured arrival are left out.

first_day.description: The earliest service day in the data, as YYYY-MM-DD.

last_day.description: The latest service day in the data, as YYYY-MM-DD.

days.description: How many service days have data.

lines.description: Every line, with bus lines before rail lines, and shorter line numbers before longer ones.

line.description: The line id, as in Metro's timetable. It names the line's file, lines/<line>.json.

agency.description: Which Metro feed the line is in. LACMTA is bus and LACMTA_Rail is rail. The same line id could appear in both.

label.description: The name riders use. The route number for a bus, such as 720, and the line name for rail, such as Metro A Line.

via.description: The corridor the line runs along, in title case. Empty for rail.

n.description: Arrivals with a measured delay, over all days.

sched.description: Scheduled stops over all days, measured or not. Divide n by this for coverage.

med.description: Median delay in seconds. Positive means late and negative means early.

p90.description: 90th percentile delay in seconds. One measured arrival in ten was later than this.

pct5.description: Percent of measured arrivals more than 300 seconds late, to one decimal place.

ontime.description: Percent of measured arrivals from 60 seconds early to 300 seconds late, both included, to one decimal place. HowLate scores the arrival at every scheduled stop. Metro scores timepoints and rail terminals only, so this is not Metro's published on-time performance.

to.description: Where each measured direction is signed for, in direction order. An empty string means the timetable names no destination.
